speaker: Unknown
en: We're going to talk a little bit about deep agents for the people here that are here for the first time, not familiar with them as a concept.

speaker: Unknown

speaker: Unknown
en: So gonna start at the basics where we normally do, which is what are deep agents?

en: And deep agents are a harness.

speaker: Unknown
en: And the first question that you might have is, what is a harness?
zh: 你可能有的第一个问题是，什么是挽具？

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, the easiest way to think about it is that when you have an agent, whether you're building it, you're talking about it, you're testing it, the agent is a model, a foundational LLM.
zh: 嗯，思考它最简单的方式是，当你有一个智能体时，无论你是在构建它、谈论它、还是在测试它，该智能体是一个模型，一个基础 LLM。

speaker: Unknown
en: Plus a harness.
zh: 加上一个挽具。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so again, the easiest way to think about this equation is that if you're not the model, you're the harness.
zh: 所以同样地，思考这个等式最简单的方式是，如果你不是那个模型，你就是那个挽具。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so the harness is everything that's built around the model to make it useful, to make it reliable, to make it good.
zh: 所以挽具是围绕模型构建的所有内容，以使其有用、可靠、良好。

speaker: Unknown
en: So if you use Claude Code, Claude Code has something like 500,000 lines of code as part of its source code.
zh: 所以如果你使用 Claude Code，Claude Code 在其源代码中包含大约 500,000 行代码。

speaker: Unknown
en: All of those 500,000 lines are part of the harness.
zh: 这 500,000 行代码全都是挽具的一部分。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so all of those lines are designed to make the model under the hood, whether that's Opus, whether that's Sonnet, whether that's something else, perform the best possible way that it can given your task.
zh: 所以所有这些代码行旨在让底层的模型，无论是 Opus、Sonnet 还是其他东西，在处理你的任务时以尽可能好的方式执行。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so what actually goes into that code?
zh: 那么实际上什么进入了那些代码？

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, there's a couple of different classes of sort of primitives that we see building up the harness.
zh: 嗯，有几种不同类型的原语构成了挽具。

speaker: Unknown
en: So a big one is going to be system prompts.
zh: 所以主要的一类将是系统提示词。

speaker: Unknown
en: That is the main interface that you have with your LLM, as well as memories.
zh: 这是你与你的 LLM 的主要接口，以及记忆。

speaker: Unknown
en: This is how you have your LLM learn over time.
zh: 这是让你的 LLM 随着时间学习的方式。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's a lot of buzz right now around dreaming and continual learning and having your LLM slowly tune itself to your preferences.
zh: 目前围绕“做梦”和持续学习、让你的 LLM 慢慢调整以适应你的偏好有很多炒作。

speaker: Unknown
en: This is usually done through memories.
zh: 这通常是通过记忆来完成的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Same thing with tools, skills, MCP, and sub-agents.

speaker: Unknown
en: All of these things that are normally part of your agent, your orchestration, are also considered part of your harness.
zh: 所有这些通常属于你的智能体的一部分、你的编排的一部分的东西，也被认为是挽具的一部分。

speaker: Unknown
en: So any of the infrastructure that you use, any of the orchestration, so file system, sandboxes, your browser, anything that the agent interacts with as part of the interface is also part of the harness.
zh: 所以你使用的任何基础设施、任何编排，如文件系统、沙箱、你的浏览器、智能体作为接口的一部分与之交互的任何东西，也是挽具的一部分。

speaker: Unknown
en: Now, the last thing that is a little bit unique to DeepAgents and is useful is the idea of hooks and middleware.
zh: 现在，最后一件事，对 DeepAgents 来说有点独特且有用的是钩子和中间件的概念。

speaker: Unknown
en: DeepAgents allows you to define your own middleware to intercept calls to the model, either before the model executes or after the model executes, so you can add in your own custom logic, things like guardrails, things like extra pre-processing or post-processing, or whatever you need to get that optimal performance for your given task.
zh: DeepAgents 允许你定义你自己的中间件来拦截对模型的调用，无论是在模型执行之前还是之后，这样你就可以加入你自己的自定义逻辑，比如护栏、额外的前处理或后处理，或者你为给定任务获得最佳性能所需的任何东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: So what's included in DeepAgent's harness?
zh: 那么 DeepAgent 的挽具中包含什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: So the way that you can think about DeepAgent is that it includes best practices when it comes to harnesses out of the box, and it's open source.
zh: 所以你可以这样看待 DeepAgent，它在开箱即用的挽具方面包含了最佳实践，并且它是开源的。

speaker: Unknown
en: So Claude Code is closed sourced if you don't count the leaks, but DeepAgent's are fully open source.
zh: 所以 Claude Code 是闭源的，如果你不算泄漏的话，但 DeepAgents 是完全开源的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so what that means is that you can tune DeepAgent as a harness to your specific use case, your specific task, and it includes a few core primitives that allow you to pull different levers and again, adjust your performance.
zh: 所以这意味着你可以将 DeepAgent 作为挽具调整到你的特定用例、你的特定任务，它包含一些核心原语，允许你拉动不同的杠杆并再次调整你的性能。

speaker: Unknown
en: So one of the biggest ones that you've probably heard me talk a lot about if you've been at previous meetups is the file system.
zh: 所以如果你参加了以前的聚会，你可能听过我谈论很多的一件大事是文件系统。

speaker: Unknown
en: The file system is...

speaker: Unknown
en: Probably the state of the art when it comes to context management today, where agents will utilize the file system to store information that they might need to reference, such as a scratch pad.
zh: 可能是当今语境管理方面的最先进技术，智能体将利用文件系统来存储它们可能需要引用的信息，比如草稿纸。

speaker: Unknown
en: And because foundational models have been trained on so much file system data in the course of optimizing Claude Code and Codex and coding agents,
zh: 而且因为基础模型在优化 Claude Code 和 Codex 以及编码智能体的过程中接受了大量文件系统数据的训练，

speaker: Unknown
en: Foundational models are very, very good at utilizing the interface, so giving your data to your model in the form of a file system tends to boost performance.

speaker: Unknown
en: Now, there's a lot of other things like summarization, subagents, and planning that are really centered around context management that DeepAgent exposes to you so that you can effectively control what information makes it to your model, and so only the minimal amount of information passes to your model as needed, so you can extend your context window and you can keep your model focused.
zh: 现在，还有很多其他事情，比如摘要、子智能体和规划，它们真正围绕语境管理，DeepAgent 将它们暴露给你，这样你可以有效地控制哪些信息传递给你的模型，因此只有最少量的信息根据需要传递给你的模型，你可以扩展你的语境窗口并保持你的模型专注。

speaker: Unknown

speaker: Unknown

speaker: Unknown
en: But in general, the direction that we're heading is that models are getting better, and the basic deep agent harness is also getting better in terms of performance.

en: You could also make the trade-off to have your model

zh: 现在让我们最后进入到讨论在生产环境中运行这些 agent 意味着什么的部分，以及当你在生产环境中有一个 agent 时可能面临的一些特殊考虑因素。

speaker: Unknown
en: Standard infrastructure in short is not really built for long running complex agents.
zh: 简而言之，标准的基础设施并不是真正为长时间运行的复杂 agent 构建的。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's not really built for deep agents.
zh: 它并不是真正为 deep agent 构建的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so it brings some additional production considerations if you want to be deploying these agents and using them for significant tasks that are relevant and important for your business.
zh: 因此，如果你想部署这些 agent 并将其用于与你的业务相关且重要的重大任务，这会带来一些额外的生产考虑因素。

speaker: Unknown
en: So some extra considerations that you have to think about is that lots of deep agent use cases are long running.
zh: 所以你需要考虑的一些额外考虑因素是，许多 deep agent 用例是长时间运行的。

speaker: Unknown
en: They're multi-step.
zh: 它们是多步骤的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And because they're long running, you do need a good way to handle errors.
zh: 而且因为它们是长时间运行的，你确实需要一个处理错误的好方法。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's likely that the longer your task is, at some point your agent is going to fail, and it's going to feel really bad if you're on step 67 out of 123, and then you have to execute all the 67 steps again when you restart the task.
zh: 你的任务时间越长，你的 agent 在某个时刻失败的可能性就越大，如果你正处于 123 个步骤中的第 67 步，然后当你重新启动任务时必须再次执行所有 67 个步骤，这感觉会非常糟糕。

speaker: Unknown
en: Same thing with autoscaling or parallel fanout, resuming drop sessions and incorporating human in the loop.

speaker: Unknown
en: There's a lot of the different considerations that you have to think about up here on this slide if you are using agents in production.

speaker: Unknown
en: And so your runtime needs to accommodate deep tasks or complex tasks or deep agents.

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm saying the word deep a lot, but you get the point of where I'm going.

speaker: Unknown
en: And so let's take a look at some of the specific considerations, zooming in on some of those from the list that we found most important when we were building our production agents at LangChain.
zh: 所以让我们来看看一些具体的考虑因素，深入探讨一下我们在 LangChain 构建生产 agent 时发现的列表中最重要的几项。

speaker: Unknown
en: So one of the first ones that I mentioned was durable execution.
zh: 所以我提到的第一件事是持久执行。

speaker: Unknown
en: As we noticed our agents getting longer and longer running, we noticed that we do have this problem where you need some way to recover from failures because
zh: 当我们注意到我们的 agent 运行时间越来越长时，我们注意到确实存在这个问题，你需要某种方式从故障中恢复，因为

speaker: Unknown
en: One of the core patterns of agents, again, is still that they're limited by their context window.
zh: agent 的核心模式之一，仍然是它们受到上下文窗口的限制。

speaker: Unknown
en: And a lot of the innovation around harnesses today is about maximizing your context window.
zh: 今天围绕 harness 的许多创新都是关于最大化你的上下文窗口。

speaker: Unknown
en: So by nature of building a complex agent, you are likely going to be pushing your context window to the limit.
zh: 因此，构建复杂 agent 的本质意味着你很可能会将你的上下文窗口推向极限。

speaker: Unknown
en: You're going to be running things for very long periods of time.
zh: 你将在很长的时间内运行事物。

speaker: Unknown
en: And somewhere in that process, as you get pushed to the limit, it's more and more likely for your agent to hallucinate, for your agent to fail, or for it to encounter some other error.
zh: 在这个过程中的某个地方，当你被推向极限时，你的 agent 产生幻觉、失败或遇到其他错误的可能性越来越大。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so it's very important to be able to recover from exactly that same spot where you had the error occur and not have to restart the task all the way from the very beginning.

speaker: Unknown

speaker: Unknown
en: We have checkpointing basically every step of your execution.

en: So if you have a failure at step 67, you can start from step 66 and not have to go back to step one.

speaker: Unknown
en: Another thing that checkpointing allows and basically storing the state at every step of execution is that if you link together all of these different associated states, you can start building this concept of memory.

speaker: Unknown
en: This is equivalent to short-term memory.

speaker: Unknown
en: And this is how agents today using our open source, using deep agents, are able to remember what you said in previous turns of a conversation.

speaker: Unknown
en: Because under the hood, we're able to associate all of those same execution steps with one single session and use that to preserve the agent's memory so that it can remember if you said your preferences five messages ago.

speaker: Unknown
en: And you can again extend this across sessions to what we call long-term memory.

speaker: Unknown
en: So deep agents, when we put them into production, we always include a long-term memory store in which we will extract insights that we want to have persist across many different sessions.

speaker: Unknown
en: The most basic use case for this that you can imagine is personalizing something for a given user.

speaker: Unknown
en: So maybe your user really likes Python for a coding agent and you want it to remember to always give its examples in Python.

speaker: Unknown
en: Those are the sorts of pieces of information that you can put into long-term memory and extract them out from all of the checkpoints that you've gathered across many, many different sessions.
zh: 这些就是你可以放入长期记忆并从你在许多许多不同会话中收集的所有检查点中提取出的那类信息。

speaker: Unknown
en: Now, more and more as we're seeing agents put into production, you also have to handle authentication.
zh: 现在，越来越多的我们看到 agent 被投入生产，你还必须处理身份验证。

speaker: Unknown
en: And this is its own unique class of problem where not only do you have users with access to tools, you also need to consider which tools should your agent have access to.
zh: 这是其自己独特的一类问题，你不仅要考虑拥有访问工具权限的用户，你还需要考虑你的智能体应该有权访问哪些工具。

speaker: Unknown
en: And this can be a little bit different from your standard authentication.
zh: 这可能与你标准的认证有点不同。

speaker: Unknown
en: So at the very basic level, you probably don't want to have your agents doing things that your user cannot do.
zh: 所以在非常基础的层面上，你可能不希望你的智能体做你的用户不能做的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: So acting on behalf of the user is, through OAuth, a pretty standard flow that, at minimum, you need to build into your agents.
zh: 所以代表用户行事，通过 OAuth，是一个非常标准的流程，至少，你需要将其构建到你的智能体中。

speaker: Unknown
en: But there's also new sorts of RBAC and auth scenarios that agents have fuzzy lines around that you don't really have with traditional applications.
zh: 但也有新型的 RBAC 和认证场景，智能体周围有模糊的界限，而你在传统应用程序中真的没有这些。

speaker: Unknown
en: For example, if I use an application that is going to talk to my Gmail today, I can give it access to read and send emails.
zh: 例如，如果我今天使用一个要与我的 Gmail 对话的应用程序，我可以授予它阅读和发送电子邮件的访问权限。

speaker: Unknown
en: And if I give it that access once, because apps today are pretty deterministic, I can feel pretty comfortable that this application can send emails whenever I want.
zh: 而且如果我一次性授予它该权限，因为今天的应用程序是非常确定性的，我可以很放心地认为，只要我想，这个应用程序就可以发送电子邮件。

speaker: Unknown
en: But that same dynamic might not be present for
zh: 但同样的动态可能不存在于

speaker: Unknown
en: For a deep agent or a more complex agent.
zh: 对于一个深度智能体或更复杂的智能体。

speaker: Unknown
en: For example, you might be okay with an agent sending one email on your behalf, but you might think that something's wrong and you might want to investigate if you see that agent sending a thousand emails on your behalf.
zh: 例如，你可能可以接受智能体代表你发送一封电子邮件，但如果你看到该智能体代表你发送一千封电子邮件，你可能会认为出了问题，并且你可能想要调查一下。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that's a different sort of auth flow than traditional applications will see.
zh: 这是一种与传统应用程序所见到的不同类型的认证流程。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so this is an area that's still being figured out.
zh: 所以这是仍在摸索中的一个领域。

speaker: Unknown
en: You have to think about, you know, what are your inbound authentication handlers?
zh: 你必须考虑，你知道，你的入站认证处理程序是什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: What are your outbound to third party handlers that you need?
zh: 你需要的出站到第三方处理程序是什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: And what is the RBAC that you need to be able to deploy and to work with your agents?
zh: 而你需要什么样的 RBAC 才能能够部署并与你的智能体一起工作？

speaker: Unknown
en: Now, the last thing that is important that I want to call out is interfacing with users because as of today, most tasks that are important still involve some degree of human in the loop.
zh: 现在，我想指出的最后一件重要的事情是与用户交互，因为直到今天，大多数重要的任务仍然涉及某种程度的人在回路中。

speaker: Unknown
en: There are cases where you can fully run something autonomously end to end with an agent, but many cases today, you will still want to have some degree of human oversight.
zh: 在某些情况下，你可以完全端到端地自主运行某事，但在今天的许多情况下，你仍然希望拥有某种程度的人工监督。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so this is something that needs to be built into your runtime and needs to be supported at a very foundational level for your agents.
zh: 所以这是需要构建到你的运行时中的东西，并且需要在非常基础的水平上为你的智能体提供支持。

speaker: Unknown
en: So with deep agents and with LangGraph and our open source, this is a core primitive that you always have accessible to you.
zh: 所以对于深度智能体和 LangGraph 以及我们的开源来说，这是一个核心原语，你始终可以访问它。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so if you deploy anything in production with deep agents or any of your own agents, you should consider
zh: 所以如果你在生产环境中部署任何东西，使用深度智能体或你自己的任何智能体，你应该考虑

speaker: Unknown
en: How is my human user going to interact with this agent?
zh: 我的人类用户将如何与这个智能体交互？

speaker: Unknown
en: How can my human user interrupt or stop or approve whatever the agent is doing?
zh: 我的人类用户如何中断、停止或批准智能体正在做的任何事情？

speaker: Unknown
en: And one of the core pieces of infrastructure is also how can I stream the agent's progress back to my human user?
zh: 基础设施的核心部分之一也是我如何将智能体的进度流式传输回给我的人类用户？

speaker: Unknown
en: Because oftentimes these agents will be running, like we said, for long periods of time, and you want to keep the human updated as to what the agent is doing and if it is still working.
zh: 因为通常这些智能体会运行，就像我们说的，很长时间，并且你想要让人类保持更新关于智能体正在做什么以及它是否仍在工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so these are all considerations that you have to think about if you're putting complex agents into production.
zh: 所以如果你要将复杂的智能体投入生产，这些都是你必须考虑的因素。

speaker: Unknown
en: It wouldn't be fitting if we noticed all of these problems and then didn't have a solution for them.
zh: 如果我们注意到了所有这些问题，却没有针对它们的解决方案，那就不合适了。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I do have to throw in this little pitch at the end where we say, we do have these problems solved with LangSmith deployments.
zh: 所以我确实必须在最后抛出这个小广告，我们会说，我们通过 LangSmith 部署解决了这些问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you are building agents and you don't want to figure out these problems yourself,
zh: 如果你正在构建智能体并且不想自己解决这些问题，

speaker: Unknown
en: We do support deployments where you can take an agent that you've built and automatically deploy it onto our platform to handle these exact scenarios that we just spent time talking about.
zh: 我们确实支持部署，你可以获取你构建的智能体并将其自动部署到我们的平台上，以处理我们刚才花时间讨论的这些确切场景。

speaker: Unknown
en: But again, whether or not you use our products, whether or not you're building with LangSmith, if you're putting stuff into production, you most likely will run into these same issues and you most likely will need to have your own solutions to these issues.
zh: 但同样，无论你是否使用我们的产品，无论你是否正在使用 LangSmith 构建，如果你将东西投入生产，你很可能会遇到这些相同的问题，并且你很可能需要拥有你自己针对这些问题的解决方案。
